mainTopic: Following רבי against a group of חכמים, and whether a בכור takes a double share of improvements, loans and interest.
overview: The amud opens by explaining why an earlier Sage was unsure whether to follow רבי. The question is whether the rule that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague also holds against a group of חכמים. רב says it is forbidden to rule like רבי. רב נחמן says it is permitted. רבא says not to do it at the start, but a ruling already made stands. Two versions of a teaching on 'בכל אשר ימצא לו' follow: one matches רבי and one matches the רבנן on whether a בכור doubles property that improved on its own. The גמרא then asks whose view two rulings follow and settles both with the רבנן. שמואל's rule gives no double share of a loan. The ruling from ארץ ישראל gives double of the loan but not the interest, because it treats a loan as already collected. אמימר taught that same ruling, and רבינא explains that he follows the approach of נהרדעא, seen in רב נחמן's view that collected money is doubled while רבה says collected land is. The amud ends as אביי begins to challenge both רבה and רב נחמן, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the earlier Sage was unsure about following רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the doubt: does the rule 'the הלכה follows רבי' apply only against one colleague, or even against several colleagues?
steps.simpleTranslation: He was unsure. Maybe the rule is that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague but not against many colleagues. Or maybe the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague and even against many colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the Sage quoted just before this did not give a clear ruling. He had a real doubt about how far a known rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an accepted rule that when רבי argues with one other תנא, we follow רבי. Here, though, רבי is arguing against the חכמים, a group. The doubt is whether רבי's authority is strong enough to beat a majority as well.

keyTerms.meaning: He was in doubt
The הלכה follows רבי against his (single) colleague
Against his colleagues (plural: a group or majority)
And even

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the tiny spelling difference. מחבירו (with a ו at the end) means one colleague, while מחביריו (with יו at the end) means many colleagues. The whole sugya turns on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This doubt sets up the three opinions that follow. Each later opinion is really an answer to this one question.

phrases.english: He was in doubt
whether the הלכה follows רבי against his colleague
but not against his colleagues;
or the הלכה follows רבי against his colleague
and even against his colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the earlier Sage's undecided ruling, which comes before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was unsure whether the rule 'הלכה כרבי מחבירו' extends to disputes against a majority of colleagues.

steps.title: רב says it is forbidden to rule like רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: you may not act according to רבי, because the rule only works against one colleague, not many.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: It is forbidden to act according to רבי's words. He holds that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague, but not against many colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first of three opinions answering the doubt. רב says we may not follow רבי here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the rule narrowly. רבי beats one opponent, but not a group. Since the חכמים are a group, we follow them, and ruling like רבי is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to act (to rule this way)
He holds (the reason behind his view)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
It is forbidden to act according to the words of Rabbi.
He holds: the הלכה follows Rabbi against his colleague
but not against his colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the doubt from step 1 by choosing the first side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ruling like רבי against a majority is forbidden, because רבי's authority only beats a single colleague.

steps.title: רב נחמן says it is permitted to rule like רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in his own name, says you may act like רבי, because the rule applies even against many colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן himself said: It is permitted to act according to רבי's words. He holds that the הלכה follows רבי against one colleague, and even against many colleagues.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second opinion. Now רב נחמן gives his own view, which is the opposite of what he quoted from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads the rule broadly. רבי's authority is so great that it beats even a group of חכמים, so following רבי is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: His own (his own opinion)
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two רב נחמן lines. In step 2 he only quoted רב. Here he gives his own opinion, and it disagrees with רב.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman himself said:
It is permitted to act according to the words of Rabbi.
He holds: the הלכה follows Rabbi against his colleague
and even against his colleagues.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to the doubt, against the view of רב in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ruling like רבי is permitted, because רבי's authority beats even a majority of colleagues.

steps.title: רבא's middle path: don't rule like רבי, but a ruling already given stands
steps.stepSummary: רבא says one should not rule like רבי, but if a judge already did, the ruling stands, because the original rule was only 'we lean' (מטין).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is forbidden to act according to רבי's words, but if someone did, what he did stands. He holds that the rule was stated as 'we lean,' not as a firm הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third opinion that sits between the first two. Before acting, don't follow רבי; after the fact, a ruling like רבי is not undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that the original teaching only said 'מטין', meaning we lean toward one side. It did not set a firm rule. So the preferred path is not to follow רבי, but a judge who did is not considered to have made a real mistake, and his ruling remains valid.

keyTerms.meaning: If he did it, it is done (the ruling stands after the fact)
We lean / incline toward (a softer guideline, not a firm rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on following רבי against a group of חכמים: רב says forbidden; רב נחמן says permitted; רבא says don't do it at the start, but if a judge did, it stands, since the rule was only 'מטין'.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's view shows a common pattern in הלכה. The ideal way to rule (לכתחילה) and what is valid after the fact (בדיעבד) can be different.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is forbidden to act according to the words of Rabbi,
but if he did, it is done.
phrases.notes: He means a judge who already ruled like רבי: his ruling is not cancelled.

phrases.english: He holds: 'we lean' was what was stated.
phrases.notes: The teaching was only 'we lean toward' one side, not a firm rule, so going the other way isn't treated as a real error.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a compromise between the two opposite positions in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not rule like רבי at the start, but a ruling already made like רבי stands, since the original guideline was only 'מטין'.

steps.title: רב נחמן's version of the teaching matches רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches that 'בכל אשר ימצא לו' excludes only improvements the heirs made themselves. Improvement that happened to the property on its own after the father died does go to the בכור as a double share. This follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן taught from the other books of the school of רב: 'Of all that is found to him' leaves out improvement that the heirs made after their father's death. But improvement that the property gained by itself after their father's death, the בכור does take. Whose view is this? רבי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching, in רב נחמן's version, that backs up רבי's view about property that improved on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the פסוק leave out only improvement caused by the heirs' own work. Natural improvement still counts for the double share of the בכור. That is exactly רבי's position, so this version supports him.

keyTerms.meaning: Improvement; an increase in the value of property
Double share, the inheritance of a בכור
Books of teachings from the school of רב that explain the פסוקים
Excluding; this leaves out
And whose view is this?

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two kinds of שבח apart. One is improvement the heirs made with their own work. The other is improvement the property gained by itself, like a crop growing. רבי and the רבנן argue only about the second kind.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman taught
in the other books of the school of Rav:
phrases.notes: These are collections of teachings that explain the פסוקים of the תורה.

phrases.english: "Of all that is found to him"
excludes improvement that the heirs brought about
after their father's death.
But improvement that the property gained on its own
after their father's death, he does take.
phrases.notes: He means the בכור takes his double share of it.

phrases.english: And whose view is this? It is Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב נַחְמָן בִּשְׁאָר סִפְרֵי דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source version that supports רבי's side of the debate discussed in the earlier steps.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that a בכור takes a double share of property that improved on its own after the father's death
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's version of the ברייתא on 'בכל אשר ימצא לו'

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's version of the teaching matches the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא teaches the opposite version. The פסוק excludes even improvement that happened to the property on its own, and all the more so improvement the heirs made. This follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא taught from the other books of the school of רב: 'Of all that is found to him' leaves out improvement the property gained by itself after the father's death. All the more so, the בכור does not take improvement the heirs made after their father's death. Whose view is this? The רבנן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same teaching, and this one matches the רבנן instead of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק leaves out natural improvement too. Improvement from the heirs' own work is then left out 'all the more so' (כל שכן). So the two traditions of the same teaching contradict each other: one backs רבי, the other backs the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And all the more so
The Sages, the majority view arguing with רבי

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama taught
in the other books of the school of Rav:
"Of all that is found to him"
excludes improvement that the property gained on its own
after their father's death,
and all the more so improvement that the heirs brought about
after their father's death, that he does not take.
And whose view is this? It is the Rabbis.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the same teaching. רב נחמן's matches רבי, so natural improvement is included. רמי בר חמא's matches the רבנן, so natural improvement is excluded.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא בִּשְׁאָר סִפְרֵי דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the same teaching, which supports the רבנן against רבי.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that a בכור does not take a double share even of natural improvement
steps.raayaSupportSource: רמי בר חמא's version of the ברייתא on 'בכל אשר ימצא לו'

steps.title: שמואל: a בכור does not take a double share of a loan
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a בכור does not get a double share of money that was owed to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a בכור does not take a double share of a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. שמואל rules that debts owed to the father are not part of the בכור's double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan is money the father was owed but did not yet hold when he died. שמואל treats it as something the בכור does not take double from. The next step will ask whose view this matches.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who inherits a double share
A loan; here, money others owed the father
Takes

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בַּמִּלְוָה.
phrases.english: A firstborn does not take a double portion of a loan.
phrases.notes: He means a debt that someone owed the father when he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement related to the same laws of the בכור's share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור does not take a double share of debts owed to the father.

steps.title: Whose view is שמואל's rule? Not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view שמואל follows. If it were the רבנן, the rule would be obvious. They deny the double share even for improvement of property the father actually owned, so a loan, which he never held, would surely be excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say the רבנן: the רבנן already say he does not take improvement of property that was in the father's possession. Do we even need to say it about a loan?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion שמואל is following and tests the first option, the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not give a double share even of improvement to property that was in the father's possession. A loan was never in his hands at all, so it is excluded even more. שמואל would not need to teach something that obvious, so he cannot be following the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
If you say...
In his possession
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say according to the Rabbis,
now, improvement of property that was in his possession,
phrases.notes: "His" means the father's. The property itself was his when he died.

phrases.english: the Rabbis say he does not take;
is it necessary to say a loan?!

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the רבנן agree with שמואל. They certainly do. The problem is that for them his rule would be too obvious to need saying.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion שמואל's rule follows and rules out the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, רבי or the רבנן, שמואל's rule about a loan follows.

steps.title: שמואל's rule follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל is following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is according to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: שמואל's rule only adds something new if it follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives the בכור a double share of property that improved on its own. Someone might think he would also give a double share of a loan. שמואל teaches that even רבי agrees a loan is not included, because it was not in the father's possession when he died.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the גמרא switches to the other option

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule, no double share of a loan, follows רבי. Even רבי, who includes natural improvement, does not include debts owed to the father.

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by choosing רבי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule follows רבי. He gives a double share of natural improvement but not of a loan.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits neither רבי nor the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל follows רבי, then neither רבי nor the רבנן give a double share of a loan. So a ברייתא that gives the בכור double of both the loan and the interest has no one left to follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the ברייתא that teaches: 'If the sons inherited a loan document, the בכור takes a double share of both the loan and the interest.' Whose view is that? It is neither רבי nor the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion of Step 9 by bringing a ברייתא that gives the בכור a double share of a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said שמואל follows רבי, so even רבי would deny a double share of a loan. The רבנן deny it all the more, since they deny it even for improvement of property the father owned. That leaves no one who could hold the ברייתא's ruling of a double share of the loan and the interest.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document, a written record that someone owes money
The loan itself, the original amount lent
Interest paid on top of the loan
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: But then, that which was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: The 'but then' means: if שמואל really follows רבי, as Step 9 said.

phrases.english: If they inherited a loan document,
the firstborn takes a double share,
both of the loan and of the interest.
Whose view is this?
It is neither רבי nor the רבנן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 9 that שמואל follows רבי
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that שמואל follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even רבי denies a double share of a loan, then the ברייתא granting double of the loan and the interest fits no one.

steps.title: שמואל really follows the רבנן, and his rule was still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back and says שמואל follows the רבנן after all. His rule was not obvious, because we might have thought a loan backed by a document counts as already collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, שמואל follows the רבנן, and he still needed to say it. You might have thought that a loan, since the lender holds the document, is as if it were already collected. So שמואל teaches us it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by switching שמואל back to the רבנן. It explains why his rule still needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 had rejected the רבנן because then שמואל's rule would be obvious. Now the גמרא says it is not obvious: holding the document might make the loan count as money already in the father's hands. שמואל teaches that it does not count that way. This leaves the ברייתא free to follow רבי, though the גמרא does not say so in these words.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (going back to an earlier option)
It was needed to say it
You might have thought
It is like money already collected
So it teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא follows the רבנן here. It is שמואל who is now placed with the רבנן. The ברייתא, which gives a double share, fits רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: שמואל, who says no double share of a loan, follows the רבנן. The ברייתא, which gives double of the loan and the interest, follows רבי.

phrases.english: Really, it follows the רבנן, and it was needed,
phrases.notes: 'It' is שמואל's rule from Step 7, not the ברייתא.

phrases.english: since you might have thought:
a loan, since he holds the document,
is like money already collected;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by reversing Step 9's matching
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassignment of the view plus a 'needed to say it' explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A loan backed by a document might count as money already in the father's possession, so even the רבנן would give double.
steps.terutzMaskana: A loan is not counted as collected, so according to the רבנן the בכור gets no double share. שמואל follows the רבנן, and the ברייתא can follow רבי.

steps.title: Ruling from ארץ ישראל: double of the loan but not the interest
steps.stepSummary: A ruling sent from ארץ ישראל says the בכור takes a double share of the loan itself but not of the interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there (ארץ ישראל): the בכור takes a double share of the loan, but not of the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from ארץ ישראל that splits the loan from the interest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a middle position. The original loan amount gets a double share, but the interest, which was only due to the father, does not. It differs from both שמואל (no double at all) and the ברייתא (double of both).

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל
A double share

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל, where the scholars sent rulings to בבל.

phrases.english: The firstborn takes a double share of the loan,
but not of the interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling on the same topic of loans and the בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור gets a double share of the loan itself, but not of the interest.

steps.title: Whose view is the ruling from ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ruling follows. It cannot be the רבנן, since they deny a double share even for improvement of property the father owned, so surely they would deny it for a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say the רבנן: they say he does not take double even of improvement to property the father owned. Is it even a question that he would not take double of a loan?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which view the ruling from ארץ ישראל follows, and rules out the רבנן. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן deny a double share even for improvement of property that was in the father's possession. A loan was never in his possession, so the רבנן would surely deny a double share of the loan too. But the ruling gives double of the loan, so it cannot be the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Improvement, increase in value
In his possession
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say it follows the רבנן,
now, improvement of property that is in his possession,
the רבנן say he does not take double;
is it even a question about a loan?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose view the ruling of Step 12 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which view, רבי or the רבנן, the ruling from ארץ ישראל follows, after ruling out the רבנן

steps.title: The ruling must follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: Since the ruling cannot follow the רבנן, the גמרא suggests it follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from the last step. If the ruling is not the view of the רבנן, it must be the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gives the בכור a double share even of property that was not yet fully in the father's hands. So a ruling that gives a double share of a loan seems to fit רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, instead

phrases.english: Rather, it follows רבי.
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the ruling sent from ארץ ישראל in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by giving the ruling to רבי.

steps.title: But רבי gives a double share of the interest too
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי gives the בכור a double share of both the loan and the interest, while the ruling gives none for interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי, is there no double share of the interest? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, the בכור takes a double share of both the loan and the interest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. רבי gives a double share even of the interest, but the ruling says the interest is not doubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has two parts: double for the loan, and nothing extra for the interest. רבי agrees with the first part but not the second. So the ruling cannot be רבי's view either.

keyTerms.meaning: interest on a loan
a loan (the amount lent)
a double share

phrases.english: And according to רבי, not of the interest?!
But it was taught: רבי says:
A firstborn takes a double share
both of the loan and of the interest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 14 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ruling from ארץ ישראל follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי gives a double share of the interest, but the ruling denies a double share of the interest, so they do not match.

steps.title: It follows the רבנן, since a loan counts as already collected
steps.stepSummary: The ruling follows the רבנן, who treat a loan as if it were already collected, so the loan is doubled but the interest is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is the view of the רבנן, and a loan is treated like something already collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the רבנן. It explains that, for this ruling, a loan counts as money the father already had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן only give a double share of what the father already owned. The ruling holds that a loan counts as already collected, so it is doubled. The interest does not count as already collected, so it is not doubled.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (going back to an earlier idea)
it is like something already collected

steps.confusionAlert: In step 11 the גמרא said one might think a loan counts as already collected. Here the ruling from ארץ ישראל actually holds that view. That is why the רבנן can give a double share of the loan here.

phrases.english: Really, it is the רבנן,
and a loan is like something already collected.
phrases.notes: So it counts as the father's property already. The interest is not like that, so it gets no double share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by giving the ruling back to the רבנן, which also answers the problem raised in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the ruling and explains how it fits the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן never give a double share of a loan, so the ruling cannot be theirs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling follows the רבנן and holds that a loan counts as already collected, while the interest does not.

steps.title: אמימר taught the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב tells רבינא that אמימר came to his town and taught that the בכור doubles the loan but not the interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב said to רבינא: אמימר came to our place and taught that a בכור takes a double share of a loan, but not of the interest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report comes in: a later sage, אמימר, taught the same rule as the ruling from ארץ ישראל. This sets up רבינא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same: double for the loan, nothing extra for the interest. The question now is why אמימר ruled this way.

keyTerms.meaning: he happened to come, he visited
he taught publicly
to our place

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב אחא בר רב said to רבינא:
אמימר came to our place and taught:
A firstborn takes a double share of a loan,
but not of the interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב לְרָבִינָא: אִיקְּלַע אַמֵּימָר לְאַתְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a later sage who taught the same ruling discussed in steps 12 to 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור takes a double share of a loan but not of its interest.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרדעא follow their usual approach
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that אמימר, a scholar of נהרדעא, is following the usual approach of his city's scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the scholars of נהרדעא are following their own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains אמימר's ruling in a few words. This line sets up the next step, which shows what the usual approach of נהרדעא is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר's ruling is not new. It matches a known approach of the נהרדעא scholars, and the גמרא is about to quote it.

keyTerms.meaning: the scholars of the city נהרדעא
following their own reasoning

phrases.english: He said to him: the scholars of נהרדעא follow their own reasoning –
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבינא. אמימר was from נהרדעא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבינא responds to the report in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר is following the usual view of the נהרדעא scholars.

steps.title: רבה and רב נחמן on debts paid in land or money
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the בכור gets a double share if the sons collected land, not money. רב נחמן says the opposite: double for money, not for land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה said: if they collected land, he has a double share; if they collected money, he does not. And רב נחמן said: if they collected money, he has a double share; if they collected land, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind רבינא's remark. The sons collected a debt owed to their father, and רבה and רב נחמן argue about when the בכור gets a double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן, a scholar of נהרדעא, gives a double share when the sons collect money. אמימר follows רב נחמן's approach, so he also gives a double share of a money loan.

keyTerms.meaning: they collected (a debt)
land
money, coins
he has (a double share)

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling from ארץ ישראל and אמימר agree: a בכור doubles the loan but not the interest. The ruling follows the רבנן because a loan counts as already collected. אמימר follows רב נחמן of נהרדעא, who gives a double share when money is collected.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רב נחמן say exact opposites. Keep them straight: רבה doubles land and not money, while רב נחמן doubles money and not land.

phrases.english: As רבה said:
If they collected land, he has a double share,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the sons collecting a debt owed to their father. 'He' is the בכור.

phrases.english: if they collected money, he does not have one.
And רב נחמן said:
If they collected money, he has a double share,
if they collected land, he does not have one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה: גָּבוּ קַרְקַע יֵשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבינא's claim in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That אמימר's ruling matches the usual approach of the נהרדעא scholars.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבה and רב נחמן, where רב נחמן gives a double share when money is collected.

steps.title: אביי says both opinions are difficult
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רבה that his own view and רב נחמן's view each have a problem, and he begins to explain the problem with רבה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: According to you there is a difficulty, and according to רב נחמן there is also a difficulty. According to you there is a difficulty...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a challenge against both רבה and רב נחמן together. This line sets up his next move, where he will explain exactly what is wrong with each view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, רבה and רב נחמן ruled opposite ways about whether the בכור doubles collected land or collected money. אביי does not side with either one. He says each opinion runs into its own problem, and he starts with the one held by רבה, the person he is speaking to.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, by your own view
It is difficult, there is a problem

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the two views clash with each other. He is saying each view has its own separate problem.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabba:
According to you, it is difficult,
according to Rav Naḥman, it is difficult.
According to you, it is difficult,
phrases.notes: Now אביי starts explaining the first problem, the one with רבה's own view. The details come in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both opinions given in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The opposite rulings of רבה (double for land) and רב נחמן (double for money)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each view has its own separate problem. The specific reasoning is laid out in the lines that follow, starting with רבה's view.
